text: In the 1860s, bank robbers stopped trying to break into vaults.
Grab the manager, march him to the bank at night, and make him open the door.
A steel vault is only as safe as the man with the key.
And a scared banker will open anything.
Then a lock maker named James Sargent had a clever idea.
Build a lock that even the banker can't open.
He built it out of parts from two kitchen clocks.
The clock kept the bolt locked, and it wouldn't release until a set hour.
In 1874, the first one went onto the vault door of a bank in Morrison, Illinois.
Unluckily for the banker, neither did he.
The robbers could threaten him, tie him up, and wait.
And today, banks still use time locks.
The best security guard turned out to be a clock.
